transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-11
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Laura Chen (Redwood SE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Jared Mills (IronHarbor CTO), Priya Rao (Head of Security), Tom Wu (Platform Eng), Elena Garcia (Procurement), Marcus Li (DevOps)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, brief):
IronHarbor is evaluating hosting options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) for inference workloads. Main gating items are SOC2/ISO evidence, SSO/SAML and RBAC integration patterns, encryption/KMS requirements (HSM?), audit log retention, and data residency. Customer requested pricing delta and a technical deep dive with benchmarks. Redwoods to supply security artifacts and schedule a PoC/bench session.

Topics discussed: SOC2/ISO certificates, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC model, audit logs & retention, KMS/HSM support, data residency and on-prem options, dedicated throughput numbers, timeline for procurement.

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir: Hey, everyone. Thanks for joining — I'm Samir from Redwood, AE. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Jared: Jared here, CTO at IronHarbor.
[00:08] Priya: Priya on security.
[00:10] Tom: Tom, platform.
[00:12] Elena: Elena, procurement.
[00:13] Marcus: Marcus, DevOps.
[00:15] Laura: Laura from Redwood SE, hi. Diego also on the line.
[00:20] Samir: Great. Agenda — security posture intake, integration constraints, and then timeline / next steps. Any additions?
[00:26] Priya: No, that'll do. High level: we need to know if you can meet our compliance checklist before we move to procurement. SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, SSO, RBAC, and KMS are must-haves.
[00:38] Samir: Totally. We'll go through how Hosted, Dedicated, and Private map to each requirement. Also we'll flag where we need info from you.
[00:45] Laura: Quick note — apologies for any audio clipping, I might jump in with technical details.

[00:51] [01:05] Jared: For context, our use case: customer support agent assist with PII redaction, model calls average 300 tokens, peak qps 1200, baseline 250 qps overnight. Latency target sub-200ms tail for UI flows. Cost is important but security gating will drive the decision.

[01:30] Laura: Got it. That qps profile helps. For Hosted we can guarantee multi-tenant separation, encrypted at rest and transit, SOC2 Type II in our doc pack; Dedicated gives you isolated GPU pools and tighter throughput SLAs; Private can be VPC or on-prem for full control. Each option changes the control plane ownership and therefore our evidence envelope.

[01:55] Priya: On evidence — can you share the SOC2 report and ISO cert? Also, do you provide AWS KMS integration or customer-managed keys? We may require an HSM backed KMS.

[02:10] Samir: Yes, we'll share the SOC2 Type II report and ISO 27001 statement of applicability. For KMS: Hosted supports Bring Your Own Key with AWS KMS; Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS and in some cases HSM-backed key stores. For Private/on-prem we integrate with your KMS or HSM — it's customer-managed. Note: some of the terminology in our docs might say "BYOK" or "CMK" — apologies, the transcript may show BYOK as by-o-k.

[02:41] Tom: If we go Dedicated, how much access do we get to logs? We need audit logs at token level for certain flows and 12 months retention.

[02:52] Diego: Good question. We surface request/response metadata and event logs (who called what model, time, route, latency, error codes). We don't store raw customer prompts in plaintext in hosted unless configured; we can provide redaction options. For Dedicated/Private we can enable full audit logs and longer retention. There are tradeoffs in volume and cost.

[03:20] Priya: When you say "we don't store raw prompts" — is that configurable per route? We have legal requirements for redaction and sometimes need to persist logs but masked.
[03:30] Laura: Yes, it's route-level config. You can set retention and masking. We also support token-level hashing or hashed identifiers if you need irreversible pseudonymization. Note: some terms in our docs got mis-transcribed before — you'll see KV cash instead of KV cache sometimes.

[03:49] [05:00] Elena: From procurement side, we need the vendor security questionnaire filled and evidence attached. How long to get SOC2 and ISO artifacts?
[05:08] Samir: I can get the SOC2 redacted copy and ISO certs over within 48 hours, so by Tuesday (2027-03-15). We'll also attach our security whitepaper and a short doc on RBAC patterns.

[05:20] Jared: On RBAC, we have a fairly strict model: least privilege, separation for prod analytics, and service accounts. Can Redwood integrate with our IdP (Okta), SAML 2.0? How granular is the RBAC?

[05:32] Laura: We support SAML 2.0 and OIDC. For Hosted we offer SSO at the org level and role mapping; Dedicated/Private allows deeper mapping to groups and attribute-based access controls. We can map SAML attributes to roles and enforce just-in-time provisioning for service accounts. We also support SCIM for user provisioning.

[05:57] Priya: We need to see sample assertion mappings and a guide. Also question about session duration and token refresh policy — we need tokens no longer than 1 hour for interactive sessions.

[06:12] Diego: We'll send the SAML guide and sample mappings. Session enforcement can be configured; for Dedicated you can set shorter token TTLs and revoke sessions via the admin APIs.

[06:25] Marcus: For Private deployment — what does the control plane look like? Is it a managed control plane over the internet or fully customer controlled? Any telemetry back to Redwood?

[06:36] Laura: For Private we offer two models: a managed control plane that talks to your VPC over a restricted channel with mutual TLS, or a fully on-prem bundle where the control plane is in your environment and Redwood provides support access over a customer-approved tunnel. Telemetry can be limited to health pings; data plane stays in your network. We'll document what minimal telemetry is needed for support.

[06:58] Jared: About data residency — some of our customers require EU-only storage for logs. Is regional hosting by default available for Hosted?

[07:08] Samir: Yes, regional Hosted endpoints are supported in EU regions; logs and data can be pinned regionally for Hosted and Dedicated. For Private, of course, it's in your network. We'll include data residency certs in the pack.

[07:23] [09:00] Priya: Encryption at rest standards? FIPS 140-2/3 compliance? If we require FIPS validated modules for encryption, can Redwood support that?

[09:08] Diego: Our Hosted KMS uses cloud provider's FIPS-enabled modules where available; Dedicated can be provisioned with FIPS mode and HSM-backed keys on request. For Private, you manage the KMS so you can ensure FIPS modules. We'll need to know if FIPS is a hard blocker.

[09:34] Priya: It is for some regulated customers. We'll flag which product lines need FIPS.

[09:40] Tom: Can we get an export of audit logs in a SIEM-friendly format, real-time? We plan to pipe logs into Splunk/Datadog.

[09:49] Laura: Yes, we support streaming audit logs via Kafka, Kinesis, or webhooks in JSONL. For Dedicated we can push directly into your VPC logging pipeline.

[10:00] Marcus: How about developer keys and rotation? We want automatic rotation and hardware-backed keys for production service accounts.

[10:08] Diego: We support short lived service tokens and integration with your KMS for key wrapping. Rotation is automated for managed keys; for BYOK you control rotation.

[10:20] [12:00] Elena: Procurement wants to know the timeline for pilot and procurement — we have Q2 budget but need vendor fit by end of March. Can Redwood commit to a PoC within two weeks?

[12:10] Samir: We can do a lightweight PoC: a two-week benchmarking PoC on Dedicated or Private depending on your choice. We'll need a scope doc and expected traffic patterns. Plan to start week of 2027-03-21.

[12:24] Jared: That aligns. We'll decide between Dedicated and Private after security artifacts and a quick cost delta.

[12:30] Priya: A couple of nuanced asks:
- We require immutability guarantees for audit logs for 12 months then archival for 7 years.
- We need a tamper-evident chain; any support for immutable ledger or signed audit entries?

[12:48] Laura: We can provide signed audit logs using HMAC signing with customer-managed keys. For higher assurance, Dedicated/Private allows write-once archival to your own object store or an immutable store. We'll document options.

[13:05] Tom: Is there an E2E encryption option where the model vendor can't see plaintext? We want to minimize plaintext surface.

[13:15] Diego: There are patterns: client-side encryption before sending tokens, but then you lose model utility. Practically, we support token redaction and partial field masking. For HSM-based key exposure controls we can minimize who in our org can decrypt logs. If you need fully E2E, we'd review use-case tradeoffs.

[13:48] [15:00] Priya: How do you handle breach notifications and incident response? SLA for notification?

[15:06] Samir: We follow our incident response playbook — for critical incidents we notify customers within 1 hour and provide a timeline of remediation. We'll include incident response annex and contact escalation list in the packet.

[15:20] Jared: Any third-party pen test reports or recent security assessments?

[15:26] Samir: Yes, we have a recent third-party pentest summary and remediation matrix. We'll include the redacted pentest report.

[15:34] Marcus: For Dedicated, what's the onboarding process and lead time for GPU pools?

[15:40] Laura: Typically 2-4 weeks for initial Dedicated provisioning depending on region and capacity; for Private/on-prem it's longer — architecture review + on-site support windows. We'll propose timelines in the next email.

[15:53] Tom: A technical question — do you support model quantization and mixed-precision on Dedicated to reduce cost?

[16:01] Diego: Yes, our runtime supports quantized variants and kernel selection to trade accuracy for throughput. We'll give you recommended configs for your 300-token average profile.

[16:12] [18:00] Elena: Procurement note — we need insurance certificates and a standard MSA; can you share standard contracting timelines?

[18:07] Samir: We'll attach our insurance Acord cert and a sample MSA. The legal cycle varies but with standard terms we see 3-6 weeks; enterprise redlines can extend.

[18:20] Priya: For SSO provisioning — do you support SCIM v2?

[18:25] Laura: Yes SCIM v2 for user provisioning is supported.

[18:30] Jared: Ok, to summarize — primary blockers: SOC2/ISO evidence, KMS/HSM support, audit log immutability and retention, SAML/SCIM integration samples. Pricing delta will determine Dedicated vs Private. PoC requested week of 3/21. Legal/procurement needs artifacts.

[18:55] Samir: That's a good recap. We'll do these items: SOC2+ISO pack, SAML/SCIM guide, RBAC sample configs, audit log export formats, and a proposed PoC scope and pricing delta.

[19:10] Priya: One last question — do you have an SLA for data deletion and verified purging? We need the ability to request deletion and get a verifiable report.

[19:18] Diego: Yes, we support deletion requests and an attestation of deletion for Hosted and Dedicated. For Private, deletion is within your environment but we can provide a verification checklist and tools to run and capture evidence.

[19:32] Elena: Great. Logistics — Samir, can you send the pack and propose 2-3 slots for the deep dive?

[19:38] Samir: Absolutely. I'll send the pack by 3/15 and propose deep-dive slots for the week of 3/21.

[19:45] Jared: Thanks all.
[19:46] Priya: Thanks.
[19:47] Laura: Thank you, we'll follow up.

End transcript.
